nodes.label: Transport interface
nodes.rationale: Small surface — bootstrap, send, receive, disconnect — so cluster behaviour is identical whichever implementation is plugged in. A competent custom implementation is ~200 lines; the hard part is matching the framing and heartbeat semantics the cluster expects.

nodes.label: TcpTransport
nodes.rationale: The production default: listens, connects lazily, auto-reconnects on the next send, and caps frame size. Unauthenticated by default — fine on a private network, but any internet path wants TLS plus a shared secret.

nodes.label: InMemoryTransport
nodes.rationale: Transports find each other through a process-global registry keyed by self address — no bus to wire. Used by MultiNodeSpec to run a multi-node cluster in one process without ports.

nodes.label: TcpBackend
nodes.rationale: One implementation per runtime (Bun.listen/connect, node:net, Deno.listen/connect), auto-detected via getTcpBackend(), so the same TcpTransport runs everywhere.

nodes.label: Frame-size cap
nodes.rationale: 16 MiB by default, to stop a DoS via a forged length prefix. Raising it does not improve general throughput — it only matters for individual large messages.

nodes.label: Connection multiplexing
nodes.rationale: Gossip, heartbeats, envelopes and subsystem traffic (sharding, pubsub gossip, DistributedData replication) share one TCP stream with no priority routing — heartbeats and bulk traffic compete. Reserving bandwidth for control traffic would need a custom transport with per-channel framing.

nodes.label: cluster-transport readiness check
nodes.rationale: peers() backs the readiness check: a node still expecting members with no connection to any of them is cut off and /ready answers 503 so the load balancer stops routing there. InMemoryTransport.peers() reports every registered transport regardless of connection state, so a test written against it cannot observe that failure.

nodes.label: What InMemoryTransport does not simulate
nodes.rationale: No network faults (delivery is reliable), no latency (synchronous within one event-loop turn) and no serialisation (messages pass by reference). To exercise the real encodeFrame/FrameDecoder round trip use TcpTransport over loopback; the CBOR codec is reachable from no cluster transport at all.
